Labeled assembly diagram of a two-panel folding ramp showing mechanical linkage and hinge details. Main elements:
- Two ramp panels joined by a central ramp hinge.
- Internal gears and gear racks (two locations) aligned near the hinge to actuate panel motion.
- Two drive arms, each mounted on cam gear pivot shafts (two shafts), with drive arm pivot pins (two pins per arm) connecting the arms to the ramp structure.
- Drive arms link the cam gear pivot shafts to the panels so that rotation of the gears/cams translates through the pivot pins and arms to fold or unfold the ramp panels.

content_text:
An eight‑position connector labeled P1 (pins A–H) supplies four control/indicator circuits plus power and ground. From P1 four separate signal conductors (recommended 14 AWG) go to:
- Signal to ramp deploy indicator
- Signal to ramp stow indicator
- User control signal to deploy ramp
- User control signal to stow ramp

Two 12 AWG conductors provide power and return:
- A 12 AWG positive feed from P1 is routed through a circuit protection device (25 A) to the battery positive terminal.
- A 12 AWG ground/return from P1 ties to the battery negative/chassis ground node.

The diagram notes the recommended wire gauges (14 AWG for the signal/indicator lines, 12 AWG for battery and ground) and shows the battery with its positive protected by the 25 A device and its negative connected to ground.
title: Wheelchair Ramp, p. 30

content_text:
Schematic of the ramp control wiring shown with the ramp in the stowed position. Main elements and relationships:

- Components:
  - Three microswitches labeled "DRIFT IN", "DRIFT OUT", and "COUNTER" (each drawn with common (C), normally open (NO) and normally closed (NC) contacts).
  - Two relays labeled STOW RELAY and DEPLOY RELAY (each with coil terminals 85 and 86 and changeover contact with common 30, normally open 87, and normally closed 87A).
  - A pulse COUNTER module with pins 1–4 (labels: COUNT, NEG, N/A, POS).
  - A PUMP motor (M) on the far right.
  - A multi-pin connector J1 at the top left providing wiring feeds.

- Wiring and functional relationships:
  - The DRIFT IN and DRIFT OUT microswitches drive the coils of the STOW and DEPLOY relays respectively: closing the appropriate microswitch completes the coil circuit (85/86) to energize that relay.
  - Each relay’s changeover contact (30 common, 87 NO, 87A NC) routes 12‑gauge conductors so the pump motor receives the appropriate polarity/connection for stow or deploy operation. In other words, the relays switch the 12‑ga lines between the NO and NC outputs to change pump direction.
  - The PUMP motor is connected to the relay-switched 12‑gauge lines (wires labeled with color/gauge codes) so relay states determine motor direction.
  - The COUNTER microswitch feeds the COUNTER module via 18‑gauge wires: the microswitch NO/NC outputs connect to the counter input (COUNT) and to ground/negative as needed (NEG/POS pins shown on the counter). The counter registers events when the counter microswitch changes state.
  - Wire gauge and color annotations (e.g., 12 GA RD, 12 GA BK, 14 GA OR/BK, 18 GA RD, etc.) are shown for each connection; J1 provides the external connector pin references for those wires.

- Overall purpose conveyed by the diagram:
  - Limit/micro switches control the stow and deploy relays, which in turn switch power polarity to the pump motor to move the ramp in or out. A counter module monitors position events via the counter microswitch. The drawing is annotated to show the ramp in its stowed position.
title: Wheelchair Ramp, p. 30

A wiring harness diagram for a motor/valve assembly showing the actuator/pump unit, its multi‑conductor cable and connectors, and the external control and feedback components with pin/wire-color tables for each device.

Key elements and connections:
- Motor/valve assembly (lower left) has a three‑wire pigtail that feeds into the main black harness. 
- Main harness terminates in a circular 8‑pin connector assembly; separate callouts label two circular connectors (CONNECTOR - P1 and CONNECTOR - J1) with full pin-to-wire‑color code tables.
- The harness continues and branches to: two relays labeled DEPLOY RELAY (RELAY‑1) and STOW RELAY (RELAY‑2), each shown as a standard relay block with an accompanying relay wire-code table; a small rectangular switch/connector (shown with three wires) and a 3‑wire inline module (top center).
- A counter module is shown with its wiring/pin code and a 4‑pin counter connector.
- Three microswitch assemblies on the right are labeled "DRIFT IN" microswitch, "DRIFT OUT" microswitch, and "COUNTER" microswitch; each has a microswitch connector callout with pin numbers and wire‑color assignments and individual quick‑disconnect connectors on the harness.
- All connectors, relays, the counter and microswitches include tabular pin assignments and corresponding wire colors so each conductor in the harness is identified and mapped to the appropriate device.

Overall the diagram maps each conductor from the actuator assembly through connectors and branches to the relays, counter, switch, and three microswitches, with explicit pinouts and color codes for installation and troubleshooting.

- Check Valve: spring-loaded one-way valve (ball/poppet style) permitting flow in a single direction.

content_text:
A hydraulic schematic of a dual‑actuator system fed by a single motor‑driven pump. Key elements and connections:

- Central pump (with motor) supplies two parallel working branches (left and right).
- Each branch feeds a 4‑way, spring‑centered directional spool valve that controls a single double‑acting cylinder shown at the top. The cylinder head ports are tied to common top lines labeled "A"; the rod ports are tied to lower lines labeled "B".
- Between the two branch nodes there are two fixed restriction/orifice elements labeled ".033" and ".020" connecting the branches.
- Each branch contains a spring‑biased check/sequence element (black filled triangle with spring) adjacent to the orifices.
- Pressure relief/limit valves are fitted on each pump outlet branch and annotated with set pressures: 1000 PSI on the left branch and 1250 PSI on the right.
- Dashed pilot lines and spring symbols on the spool valves indicate pilot or spring return actuation and external pilot connections between components.

Overall function conveyed: a single pump supplies two independently controlled cylinder circuits with inter‑branch flow restrictions and distinct pressure relief settings.
title: Wheelchair Ramp, p. 32

content_text: A hydraulic schematic-style exploded illustration showing two single-rod cylinders (items 1 and 2) connected by four flexible hydraulic hoses (items 4, 5, 6, 7) to a hydraulic power/valve assembly with electric motor (item 3). Hoses 4 and 5 run from the valve block to the left cylinder (1); hoses 6 and 7 run from the valve block to the right cylinder (2). Each cylinder's port is fitted with a 90° swivel/pipe fitting (item 8) where the hose attaches; the valve block end of each hose uses a set of elbow/adaptor fittings (items 9 and 10) to connect into the valve ports. Dashed lines indicate the individual fittings that attach to each hose end and the connection points on the cylinders and valve block. The drawing emphasizes component identities and the routing/connections between cylinders, hoses, fittings, and the hydraulic power/valve unit.

content_text: Maintenance and Lubrication ScheduleProper maintenance is necessary to ensure safe, troublefree operation. Inspecting the lift for any wear, damage or other abnormal conditions should be a part of the transit agency daily service program. Simple inspections can detect potential problems.The maintenance and lubrication procedures specified in this schedule must be performed by a BraunAbil- ity authorized service representative at the scheduled intervals according to the number of cycles.BraunAbility dual parallel arm lifts are equipped with hardened pins and self-lubricating bushings to de- crease wear, provide smooth operation and extend the service life of the lift.When servicing the lift at the recommended intervals, inspection and lubrication procedures specified in the previous sections should be repeated. Clean compo- nents and the surrounding area before applying lubri- cants. Clean only with water, and then when cleaned, lubricate as directed in the lubrication diagram. Do not use solvents to clean.LPS2 General Purpose Penetrating Oil is recom- mended where Light Oil is called out. Use of improper lubricants can attract dirt or other contaminants which could result in wear or damage to the components. Platform components exposed to contaminants when lowered to the ground may require extra attention.Lift components requiring grease are lubricated during assembly procedures. When these components are replaced, grease must be applied during installa- tion procedures. Specified lubricants are availablefrom BraunAbility (part numbers provided on previous page).A WARNINGMaintenance and lubrication procedures must be performed as specified by an authorized service technician. Failure to do so may result in serious bodily injury and/or property damage.All listed inspection, lubrication and main- tenance procedures should be repeated at 750 cycle intervals fol- lowing the scheduled 4500 cycle maintenance procedures. content_text: Certification Checklist Diagnostic ProceduresThe following operations and conditions must be functionally verified in order for the lift to be FMVSS 403/404 compliant. If an operation does not function as described or a condition is not met, follow the refer- enced procedures to correct the problem or contact BraunAbility Aftersales.· Vehicle movement is prevented unless the lift door is closed, ensuring the lift is stowed.1. Verify on the pump module mounted interlock connecter that the lift stowed signal - pin 9 has a ground signal OR lift not stowed signal - pin 5 has an open signal (depends on interlock used).2. Refer to the interlock installation instructions.· Lift operation shall be prevented unless the vehicle is stopped and vehicle movement is prevented.1. Verify vehicle secure signal (pin 6) has a +12 volt signal.2. Refer to the interlock installation instructions.· The platform will not fold/stow if occupied.- Refer to Platform Fold Pressure Adjustment procedures.· The inner roll stop will not raise if occupied.- Call BraunAbility Aftersales.· The outer barrier will not raise if occupied.- Refer to Outer Barrier Fold Pressure Adjustment procedures.· Verify platform lighting when lift is deployed and pendant illumination when lift is powered.1. Replace bulb(s) in the light housing.· A warning will activate if the threshold area is occupied when the platform is at least 1" below floor level.1. Remove the threshold warning plate.2. Verify the threshold strip switch connector is securely connected.3. Reinstall threshold warning plate.4. Test threshold warning (push down on plate). If warning is not activated, see Step 5.5. Remove the threshold warning plate and replace non-functioning threshold switch.6. Repeat Step 4. - Multiple tees and check/shutoff fittings route and isolate supply between front and rear circuits and between components for charging, protection, and serviceability.

The diagram emphasizes the flow path from compressor → reservoirs → dryer/separator → control/manifold → individual wheel brake connections, with valves and drains placed for protection, isolation, and maintenance.

A schematic pneumatic system diagram for a Grande West vehicle showing compressors, air treatment, storage tanks and the interconnecting DOT pipe runs (pipe diameters are indicated in the diagram legend).

Main components and flow:
- Compressor assembly (bottom left) discharges into a condenser, then an air dryer and a filter before the treated air is routed into the vehicle piping.
- Multiple air reservoirs are shown: Primary, Secondary, Auxiliary and two Suspension tanks. Each reservoir has a drain valve and is connected into the piping network via fittings and check valves.
- Tanks are interconnected with T‑fittings and straight/90° fittings so air can flow between sources and service lines; check valves prevent backflow.
- A main feed includes an 80 PSI protection valve that protects downstream circuits.
- Service branches supply suspension tanks and other vehicle services; separate small lines run to driver’s seat, transmission and front door emergency air release valves.
- The diagram labels fittings and components with numbers 1–18 (legend lists items such as air reservoir, drain valve, condenser, air dryer, check valve, filter, various fittings, compressor discharge hose, coupling, plug and the 80 PSI protection valve).

Piping notation:
- The drawing uses distinct line styles to denote different DOT pipe sizes (e.g., 1/4", 5/8", and 1/2" DOT pipe runs), matching the legend.

Overall, the diagram depicts the treatment and storage sequence (compressor → condenser → dryer → filter → reservoirs), the interconnection of multiple reservoirs, and the protected distribution of compressed air to vehicle systems via specified fittings and pipe sizes.

Key content and relationships:
- Overall assembly: caliper body (1) mounted on a carrier (2) that houses the disc rotor (46) and two brake pads (12) positioned on either side of the disc.
- Pad actuation: tappet and boot assemblies (13) and tappets/tappet bushes (161) push the pads toward the disc; springs (27, 28) and pad retainer (11/44) locate and preload the pad assemblies.
- Sliding/mounting hardware: guide pins (4b, 5) with rubber/brass bushes (6b, 6c, 7) and boots (9, 10) permit caliper movement on the carrier; threaded tube (16) and bridge (17) are shown in the caliper structure.
- Actuation and self-adjust: a brake chamber (18) drives a lever (19) and eccentric bearing (20) that engage an adjuster unit (23). The adjuster includes a chain (30), chain wheel (32), turning device (24) and adjuster cap (37) to rotate tappets and maintain pad-to-disc clearance as pads wear.
- Ancillary parts: wear sensor (33), outer boot clip (31), O-ring (31a), various bolts (39, 40, 43), washer (45), cap (68) and shear adapter (61) are identified and located.
- Insets and detail view: a zoomed cross-section of the adjuster/lever interface shows the adjuster mechanism and its linkage to the brake chamber; dashed outline indicates the external actuator housing.

content_text:
A control schematic for a front door actuator showing how a multi-position door-control switch, safety logic, and valve modules drive open/close solenoids and a pneumatic shuttle valve.

Key elements and connections:
- A rotary door control switch with multiple positions mapped to commands (open front door, close front door, open/close rear/front combinations). A note states “close front door” is interpreted as the absence of an open-front-door signal.
- Switch outputs run to a DPS input (door position/safety input) and to two VMM3 modules. The switch provides a signal to DPS when rotated to the second position.
- If safety conditions are met, the VMM modules output a 24 V signal to either the front-door-open or front-door-close solenoid depending on switch position.
- Each solenoid output drives a pilot that actuates a shuttle valve; the shuttle valve directs pneumatic air to the door actuator/motor to produce the chosen motion.
- Solenoid actuation is time-limited to 250 ms to extend solenoid life. Ground/common reference is shown for the control circuits.

Overall, the diagram links operator switch positions through safety logic and VMM outputs to timed solenoid pulses that pilot a shuttle valve, which in turn routes air to the door motor to open or close the front door.
title: Vicinity Service Manual, p. 137

content_text:
A pneumatic emergency-release and door-actuation schematic showing the components and how they connect:

- Auxiliary reservoir at bottom right supplies pneumatic pressure into the system.
- Supply line from the reservoir passes through a check valve (arrow marked "free flow") to prevent backflow, then reaches an Outside Release Valve labeled "Located behind R/Hand Headlight."
- The Outside Release Valve output continues to a Driver Release Valve (push-button style, located at the driver's seat area). From the Driver Release Valve the line continues upward and splits:
  - One branch goes to an Emergency Release at the entrance door (a local release device).
  - The main branch goes to a Double Solenoid Valve, then through a Slow Start Valve, and finally to the Door Motor actuator.
- The Door Motor assembly includes a Flow Control Valve for regulating door motion.

Overall function indicated: the auxiliary pressure is routed through a sequence of release valves (outside, driver, entrance) and control valves (double solenoid, slow-start, flow control) to operate and control the door motor; the check valve ensures correct flow direction.

- Operator cover: the housing at the bottom (operator cover) encloses the connector and provides the main mounting interface for the arm assemblies; multiple bolts secure the cover to the housing.

Fasteners (bolts, washers) are indicated throughout for securing each component and showing the order of assembly.

content_text:
A schematic of an engine coolant and DEF (diesel exhaust fluid) thermal management system showing components, flow paths, and control valves. Key components shown: engine, radiator, expansion tank, heat exchanger, transmission oil cooler, DEF tank and dosing unit, and a vertical manifold of supply/return lines with multiple branch valves. A legend identifies four circuit types: By-pass Coolant Flow, Main Coolant Flow, DEF Coolant Flow, and Vent System.

Main relationships and flows:
- Main coolant loop: coolant leaves the engine, passes through the vertical manifold and expansion tank connection, and is directed to the radiator for cooling before returning to the engine. The expansion tank ties into the main loop and provides venting and makeup flow.
- By-pass circuit: a bypass route from the engine/manifold returns some flow directly to the engine or through the heat exchanger and transmission oil cooler when radiator flow is restricted (e.g., warm-up or controlled routing). Valves on the manifold open/close to select bypass versus full-radiator flow.
- DEF coolant branch: a controlled branch taps the main loop via a set of valves and circulates coolant through the DEF tank and dosing unit to heat or maintain DEF temperature; this branch rejoins the main return. The dosing unit is connected to the branch and its inlet/outlet are shown as part of the DEF coolant loop.
- Transmission oil cooler and heat exchanger are integrated into the bypass/main routing so they receive coolant depending on valve positions.
- Vent system: vents from the expansion tank and selected branch points route air back to the expansion tank/vent network to prevent air entrapment; arrows indicate vent flow direction toward the expansion tank/vent.

Control elements:
- Several valves and check valves are placed at branch points (manifold and DEF tank connections) to regulate routing between radiator, bypass, transmission cooler, and DEF subsystem.
- The schematic emphasizes how valve positions route coolant either through the radiator or via bypass branches and how a separate, valve-controlled circuit conditions the DEF tank/dosing unit using engine coolant.

Assembly relationships: the top, bottom and vertical panels form a rectangular housing with multiple circular fan openings; the radiator slides into this housing and is sealed by the cassette assembly; the fan shroud mounts to the housing so cooling fans align with the openings; mounting hardware secures the complete assembly to its support structure.

content_text: BAULTAR CONCEPTProcédure de maintenance du siège de conducteur d'autobus AS98-5005 - Baultar Solution RTCMises en garde :Valve de nivellementDANGERNe pas modifier le mécanisme de la valve de nivellement ou alterer son fonctionnement normal.Ne pas Manipuler le levier de la valve de façon a commander l'alimentation en pression d'air du ballon lorsque le siège est en position haute.AUTREMENT, DES RISQUES IMPORTANTS DE BLESSURES PEUVENT EN RÉSULTERBallon suspension (airspring)DANGERNe pas permettre le gonflement du ballon s'il n'est pas bien en place dans la cavité de la structure du siège ainsi que s'il n'est pas utilisé dans sa hauteur et condition de design.Pression maximum du circuit pneumatique de nivellement: 60 psi lorsque le ballon est bien inséré dans sa cavité et sous les conditions prévues d'utilisation. Le ballon peut ne pas soutenir cette pression en dehors des conditions normales d'utilisation.Ne pas Manipuler le levier de la valve de nivellement de façon a commander l'alimentation en pression d'air du ballon lorsque le siège est en position haute.AUTREMENT, DES RISQUES IMPORTANTS DE BLESSURES PEUVENT EN RÉSULTERBallon d'élévationDANGERNe pas permettre le gonflement du ballon s'il n'est pas bien en place dans la cavité de la structure du siège ainsi que s'il n'est pas utilisé dans sa hauteur et condition de design.Pression maximum du circuit pneumatique d'élévation : 60 psi lorsque le ballon est bien inséré dans sa cavité et sous les conditions prévues d'utilisation avec le système de sécurité fonctionnel. Le ballon peut ne pas soutenir cette pression en dehors des conditions normales d'utilisation.Ne pas commander l'alimentation en pression d'air du ballon si le dispositif de sécurité a été altere ou n'est plus fonctionnel.AUTREMENT, DES RISQUES IMPORTANTS DE BLESSURES PEUVENT EN RÉSULTERDate : 2007-11-09 Doc. title: RP-01-33-00-00-002 Wheel Replacement, p. 1

content_text: E LIONRepair Procedure: Wheel ReplacementPROCED. #:RP-01-33-00-00-002Publication Date:2022-08-29Page 2 of 4SAFETY PRECAUTIONSWhen working on the vehicle, make sure the starter switch is in the "OFF" position, the parking brake is set, and the tires are chocked. Before working under the vehicle, always place jack stands under the frame rails to ensure the vehicle cannot drop. Failure to follow these steps can cause serious injuries or death.Tools used when working near batteries or electrical connections must be certified to a rating of 1000 Vdc to prevent injuries from electric shock. Short circuits between components or wires must be avoided.MAINTENANCE REFERENCETo be done during work that requires the replacement of wheels.DURATIONThe duration of the repair procedure is approximately 30 minutes.LIST OF MATERIAL· Wheel as specified by the manufacturerTOOLS· Heavy-duty wheel puller· Pneumatic impact spanner· Torque wrench 0 - 500 ft-lb (0 - 680 Nm)CONSUMABLES· Rags or paper towels
title: RP-01-33-00-00-002 Wheel Replacement, p. 2

content_text: 1 LIONRepair Procedure: Wheel ReplacementPROCED. #:RP-01-33-00-00-002Publication Date:2022-08-29Page 3 of 4PROCEDURE1. Make sure the work can be done safely.2. Make sure the vehicle is parked on a flat surface.3. Remove the wheel as per MP-05A-33-00-00-001 Wheel Removal.!CautionWhen replacing a wheel, remove any rust or dirt from the vehicle parts to which the wheel is attached. In an emergency, a cloth or paper towel can be used, but use a scraper or wire brush later to remove all rust and dirt.4. Remove all rust and dirt from the wheel bolts, mounting surfaces, and the replacement wheel (Figure 2).Figure 2 - Cleaning of Wheel Component5. Inspect the condition of the wheel, especially the hub. If any anomaly is found, replace the part.
title: RP-01-33-00-00-002 Wheel Replacement, p. 3

content_text: E LIONRepair Procedure: Wheel ReplacementPROCED. #:RP-01-33-00-00-002Publication Date:2022-08-29Page 4 of 4PROCEDURE (Continued)6. Install the new wheel, making sure that the valve body is facing outwards.İCaution Never use oil or grease on bolts and nuts. This may cause the nuts to loosen. The wheels of the vehicle may fall off and cause a collision. If there is any sign of wear or deformation of the wheel studs, replace the defective part. Replace any wheel that has enlarged or deformed stud housings in any way.7. Reinstall the wheel nuts and tighten them with the torque wrench until the wheel fits on the hub. Refer to MP-05A-33-00-00-003 Verification of the Wheel Nuts.8. Lower the vehicle taking every precaution for your safety. Note: Retighten the wheel nuts to the prescribed torque after 100 miles (160 km) after any service (tire rotation, flat tire replacement, or wheel removal).
title: RP-01-33-00-00-002 Wheel Replacement, p. 4

content_text: 1 LIONRepair Procedure: Replacement of the Brake Pads (Hydraulic Brake)PROCED. #:RP-01-35-01-00-005Publication Date:2022-08-24Page 3 of 5PROCEDURE1. Make sure the work can be done safely.2. Make sure the vehicle is on a flat surface.3. Raise the vehicle so the wheels that need to be serviced are off the ground. Support the vehicle with a safety stand. Block the remaining wheels.4. Verify the brake fluid level to make sure that, when the pistons are compressed, the reservoir will not be overflowing. If necessary, remove some brake fluid. Note: The reservoir is behind the front hood.5. Remove the wheel assembly to get access to the brake system.6. Remove the brake pads retainer spring bolt (Figure 2).Brake pad retainer spring boltBrake pad EdgeFigure 2 - Brake Pad Retainer Spring Bolt Location7. Insert two common screwdrivers under the brake pad edges. Work the pads out evenly to avoid binding.8. Removes all brake pads.
title: RP-01-35-01-00-005 Brakes Pads Replacement (Hydraulic), p. 3

content_text: E LIONRepair Procedure: Replacement of the Brake Pads (Hydraulic Brake)PROCED. #:RP-01-35-01-00-005Publication Date:2022-08-24Page 4 of 5PROCEDURE (Continued)!Caution Avoid placing direct pressure on a piston as damage to the component can result.9. Compress the piston on each side. Use a steel plate stock over the pistons to distribute the load uniformly (Figure 3).Figure 3 - Pistons Compression10. Inspect the rotor for scoring, warping, cracks, bluing, heat spots, or other damages or defects. Check also for minimum thickness. If necessary, repair or replace them, as per RP-03-35-00-00-009 Replacement of Brake Disks.11. Inspect the calipers for leakage, damage, or defect to piston boots, seals, or pistons. If necessary, replace or repair the defective parts as per RP-03-35-00-00-006 Caliper Replacement.12. Clean and inspect the lining wear plates. Replace the worn wear plates. Note: The inboard and the outboard brake pads are identical, except when they are equipped with a mechanical wear sensor.
title: RP-01-35-01-00-005 Brakes Pads Replacement (Hydraulic), p. 4

content_text: D LIONRepair Procedure: Replacement of the Brake Pads (Hydraulic Brake)PROCED. #: RP-01-35-01-00-005Publication Date:2022-08-24Page 5 of 5PROCEDURE (Continued)13. Install the new brake pads. Install pads equipped with a mechanical wear sensor on the inboard side of the caliper. Make sure that the friction surface is against the rotor.14. Install the pad retainer spring and tighten the bolt to 9 to 12 ft-lb (12.2 to 16.3 Nm).15. Fill the master cylinder reservoir with new, clean, DOT 3 brake fluid.16. Press on the brake pedal several times to move the brakes pistons and for the lining to make contact with the brake rotors.17. Verify again the master cylinder reservoir and as necessary top it off.18. Install the wheel and lower the vehicle.19. Perform a road test before releasing the vehicle back into service.
title: RP-01-35-01-00-005 Brakes Pads Replacement (Hydraulic), p. 5

content_text: D LIONRepair Procedure: Motor Control Unit (MCU) ReplacementPROCED. #:RP-01-11-00-00-002Publication Date: 2023-04-18Page 3 of 12CONSUMABLES· 3M 1252 sealant· Abrasive paper grade 240 or finer· Conductive grease· Contact lubricant· Coolant/anti-freeze pre-diluted 50/50 red P/N 14700003PROCEDUREYDangerThis product uses differential mode capacitors between the positive high-voltage DC bus (+) and the negative high-voltage DC bus (-), and common mode capacitors between the high-voltage DC bus and the chassis. Even when the product is disconnected from the high-voltage source, these capacitors can hold a voltage high enough to cause an electric discharge or death.!Warning This Motor Control Unit (MCU) must be installed only by qualified and authorized personnel. Always use appropriate insulation and protection before manipulating the MCU even when it is disconnected from a high-voltage source.!Caution This equipment is Electro-Static Discharge (ESD) sensitive. Never touch the connector pins with your bare hand unless proper ESD equipment is worn. The internal electronics are sensitive to electrostatic discharges.

content_text:
Labeled technical diagram of a disc brake assembly showing how the caliper, pads, and hydraulic line relate to the rotor. Main elements and relationships:
- Rotor: circular disc mounted to the wheel hub; braking surface contacted by the pads.
- Caliper: housing that straddles the rotor and contains the brake pads and actuating hardware.
- Brake pads: two friction elements positioned on either side of the rotor inside the caliper; they press against the rotor to produce braking force.
- Caliper-to-support bolts: fasteners that secure the caliper assembly to the vehicle’s support/bracket.
- Brake tube and brake hose hold-down clamp bolt: the brake tube/hose supplies hydraulic fluid to the caliper; the clamp bolt secures the hose/tube to the caliper assembly.
- Brake pad retainer spring bolt: fastener that retains the pad retainer/spring and holds the pads in position within the caliper.

Overall, the diagram identifies the parts involved in applying hydraulic pressure through the brake tube/hose to actuate the caliper pistons, forcing the pads against the rotor while the caliper is secured to its support by bolts.

content_text: D LIONRepair Procedure: Replacement of the Brake Calipers (Hydraulic Brake)PROCED. #:RP-01-35-01-00-006Publication Date:2022-08-24Page 4 of 5PROCEDURE (Continued)7. Remove the brake tube from the caliper.8. Remove the four calipers to support assembly bolts. Note: Do not disassemble the four bolts joining the two halves of the caliper.9. Remove the caliper.Installation10. Inspect the caliper to be installed for leakage, damage, or defect to the piston seals or pistons. If leakage, damage, or defect is found, the disassembly of the caliper may be required.11. With the use of C-type clamps and a metal plate, retract all the pistons into the caliper.12. Install the caliper over the rotor.13. Install the washers and start the four calipers to support bolts by hand. 14. Torque the four calipers to support bolts to 320 to 360 ft-lb (433 to 488 Nm).15. Install the brake hose.16. Secure the brake hose with the brake hose hold-down clamp bolt. Torque the bolt to 9 to 12 ft-lb (12.2 to 16.3 Nm).17. Install the brake pads as per RP-03-35-00-00-005 Brake Pads Replacement.!CautionWhen bleeding a four-piston caliper, the brake fluid monitor should be monitored to make sure the system is not drained. Add brake fluid as needed to prevent damage to the components during the operation.

content_text: D LIONRepair Procedure: Replacement of the Brake Calipers (Hydraulic Brake)PROCED. #: RP-01-35-01-00-006Publication Date:2022-08-24Page 5 of 5PROCEDURE (Continued)!Caution Always add new brake fluid into the caliper. Discard the used brake fluid. Do not reuse it. Damage to components can result.Note: Each four-piston caliper is equipped with two bleed screws. To make sure air is removed from a caliper, the bleed sequence is always inboard, outboard, and repeat inboard.18. Install a section of clear, flexible tubing with a 1/4-inch inner diameter over the inboard bleeder. Insert the other end of the tubing into a container to collect the purged brake fluid. Discard the used brake fluid.19. Apply the brake to pressurize the system.20. Repeat the same procedure to the outboard bleed screw.21. Repeat the operation for the inboard screw.22. When all the air is removed from the system, tighten the bleed air screw to 17 to 22 ft-lb (12.2 to 16.3 Nm).23. Install the wheel and lower the vehicle.24. Test the braking system before returning the vehicle to service.

content_text: 3 LIONRepair Procedure: Replacement of the Drag LinkPROCED. #:RP-01-34-00-00-005Publication Date:2022-09-13Page 2 of 8SAFETY PRECAUTIONSWhen working on the vehicle, make sure the starter switch is in the "OFF" position, the parking brake is set, and the tires are chocked. Before working under the vehicle, always place jack stands under the frame rails to ensure the vehicle cannot drop. Failure to follow these steps can cause serious injuries or death.Tools used when working near batteries or electrical connections must be certified to a rating of 1000 Vdc to prevent injuries from electric shock. Short circuits between components or wires must be avoided.MAINTENANCE REFERENCEThis procedure is done in conjunction with MP-01-34-00-00-001 Drag Link Inspection.DURATIONThe duration of the repair procedure is approximately 60 minutes.LIST OF MATERIAL· Drag, link steering P/N 15301101TOOLS. Ball stud removal tool· Certified and calibrated torque wrench· Grease gun· Long-nose pliers· Measuring tape· Ratchet wrench with appropriate sockets
title: RP-01-34-00-00-005 Replacement of the Drag Link, p. 2

content_text: E LIONRepair Procedure: Replacement of the Drag LinkPROCED. #:RP-01-34-00-00-005Publication Date:2022-09-13Page 3 of 8CONSUMABLES· Castle nut· Cutter pin· Grade 1 or grade 2 heavy-duty multipurpose lithium-based greasePROCEDURE!WarningAll steering system components are critical for a safe operation of the vehicle. Failure to maintain the steering system as specified may result in loss of steering control, which could lead to personal injury and property damage.1. Make sure the work can be done safely.2. Make sure the vehicle is on a flat surface.3. Make sure the wheels are facing forward (0 degree) and they are chocked.
title: RP-01-34-00-00-005 Replacement of the Drag Link, p. 3

content_text: D LIONRepair Procedure: Replacement of the Drag LinkPROCED. #: RP-01-34-00-00-005Publication Date: 2022-09-13Page 4 of 8PROCEDURE (Continued)Removal4. Locate the drag link and remove the cutter pins from the two castle nuts (Figure 2).053624-000Figure 2 - Location of the Castle Nuts5. Remove the two castle nuts from the drag link.6. With a ball stud removal tool, remove the ball stud from the Pitman arm and the one from the axle steering arm.7. Remove the drag link.Installation8. Loosen the bolt on the drag link and adjust the length of the drag link to 21.75 in. (55.25 cm) (Figure 3).
title: RP-01-34-00-00-005 Replacement of the Drag Link, p. 4

document_title: RP-01-34-00-00-005 Replacement of the Drag Link.pdf
content_text: 4 LIONRepair Procedure: Replacement of the Drag LinkPROCED. #: RP-01-34-00-00-005Publication Date: 2022-09-13Page 5 of 8PROCEDURE (Continued)3202122Figure 3 - Length of Drag Link9. Install the axle-end ball stud of the drag link through the bottom of the axle steering arm.Note: make sure the bolt and the nut of the clamp are loose. This will ease the adjustment of the length of the drag link.10. Install the castle nut finger tight.11. Slightly turn the steering wheel to align the hole of the Pitman arm.12. Install the ball stud of the drag link in the hole of the Pitman arm from the inboard side.13. Install the castle nut hand tight.14. Tighten the nut that keeps the clamp in place to 50 to 60 ft-lb (67.7 to 81 Nm).
title: RP-01-34-00-00-005 Replacement of the Drag Link, p. 5

document_title: RP-01-34-00-00-005 Replacement of the Drag Link.pdf
content_text: D LIONRepair Procedure: Replacement of the Drag LinkPROCED. #: RP-01-34-00-00-005Publication Date: 2022-09-13Page 6 of 8PROCEDURE (Continued)!WarningNever reduce a torque below the minimum to install a cutter pin. This could cause a failure in the direction system.15. Tighten the two castle nuts to 120 to 170 ft-lb (162 to 230 Nm).16. Properly install a cutter pin in each of the castle nuts (Figure 4).Figure 4 - Installation of Cutter Pin17. Tighten the bolt on the drag link to 59.74 ft-lb (81 Nm) (Figure 5).
title: RP-01-34-00-00-005 Replacement of the Drag Link, p. 6

document_title: RP-01-34-00-00-005 Replacement of the Drag Link.pdf
content_text: 3 LIONRepair Procedure: Replacement of the Drag LinkPROCED. #: RP-01-34-00-00-005Publication Date: 2022-09-13Page 7 of 8PROCEDURE (Continued)000Figure 5 - Bolt on the Drag Link18. With a grease gun, insert grease in the two grease fittings (Figure 6).Figure 6 - Location of the Grease Fittings19. Insert grease until the new grease comes out on the other side of the grease fitting.
title: RP-01-34-00-00-005 Replacement of the Drag Link, p. 7

content_text: D LIONRepair Procedure: Replacement of the Drag LinkPROCED. #:RP-01-34-00-00-005Publication Date:2022-09-13Page 8 of 8PROCEDURE (Continued)20. Make sure the steering wheel spokes are within + 10 degrees of the center when the front wheels are facing forward.21. Turn the starter switch to "START".22. Turn the steering wheel from left to right. Make sure the front wheels are turning in the same direction. Troubleshoot if this is not the case.23. Verify the alignment of the vehicle as per MP-01-31-0-0-07 Axle Alignment Verification.

content_text:
Labeled technical diagram of a leaf-spring axle suspension showing how the multi-leaf spring pack mounts between chassis hangers and the axle. Main elements and relationships:
- Spring assembly (multi-leaf pack) spans between a front spring hanger assembly and a rear spring hanger assembly, with the spring eyes supported by the hangers.
- Spring seat assembly at the spring center rests on the axle; U-bolts pass under the axle and over the spring pack to clamp the spring to the axle.
- Axle bottom cap (underside of the axle) is secured to the U-bolts with locknuts and washers.
- Top pad and bump stop assembly sit between the spring and the chassis/frame to limit travel and cushion impact.
- Longitudinal torque rod assembly connects the axle/spring assembly to the chassis to control fore–aft axle movement.
- Shock absorber links the axle/spring assembly to the frame to damp vertical oscillations.

The diagram annotates the mounting and fasteners (U-bolts, locknut and washer) and shows the relative placement of components that secure the spring pack to the axle and chassis.

content_text: GRANDE, WEST TRANSPORTATION 11VICINITY SERVICE MANUAL VERSION 1.01. Park the vehicle on dry, level ground. Block the rear wheels and shift the transmission into Neutral.2. Raise the front end of the vehicle until the tires clear the hydraulic jack, then tilt the hood.3. Remove the pressure and return lines from the steering gear and drain fluid into a drain pan.4. Wipe the area surrounding the power steering fluid reservoir cap using a clean towel.5. Remove and discard the canister filter. Note: Only the filter element needs to be discarded. The other parts may be used to secure the filter inside the reservoir assembly.6. Wipe the inside of the reservoir canister clean.7. Slowly turn the steering wheel from a full left position to full right at least three times to purge oil from the steering gear into the drain pan.8. Re-attach the pressure and return lines to the steering gear and tighten.9. Install a new filter element in the reservoir.10. Clean the reservoir cap using an approved solvent. Remove the used gasket from the cap and replace with a new one.11. Fill the reservoir with new steering fluid to the "Max" fill line.12. Start the vehicle and allow it to idle, checking the fluid level and filling as needed.13. Steer the wheels from full left to full right several times, checking the fluid level again.14. Once all fittings and hoses have been checked for leaks, shut the vehicle off and lower it.CHANGING FILTER ELEMENTBefore changing the filter element, the steering fluid reservoir needs to be drained. This can be done by removing the pressure and return lines from the steering gear and drain fluid into a drain pan.Filter locating deviceCanisterFilter elementCap1. Unscrew filter cap.2. Push down on filter locating device and turn. Pull it out of the reservoir.3. Remove filter element from locating device and discard safely.AUTHOR: ALAINA KEDANSvicinity6.8

Top up with fluid as needed while bus is running until fluid stops draining and reaches the "Max" line.MAX MINMAX MINBLEEDING STEERING GEAR! WARNINGUsed steering fluid and filter elements must be safely disposed of in accordance with local environmental regulations.Bleeding the steering gear is necessary if the steering box has been mounted in such a way that air becomes trapped in the sector shaft bore. This procedure should be followed whenever the steering box has been disassembled or replaced and can be completed as follows:1. Ensure the vehicle is stationary and on dry, level ground. Set the parking brake, block the wheels, and shift the transmission into Neutral.2. Tilt the hood and ensure that the fluid level in the reservoir is full.3. Start the engine and allow the vehicle to idle.4. Steer the wheels from full left to full right several times, ensuring that the pitman arm makes full travel.5. Open the bleeder screw located on the sector shaft bore until non-aerated fluid pours out. Do not turn the steering wheel while the bleeder is open.6. Repeat steps 3 to 5 until no aeration is found in the bleed oil, then tighten the bleed screw.7. Check the fluid level in the power steering reservoir. If no fill is necessary, shut the vehicle off, lower the hood, and remove wheel blocks.CAUTION: Excessive heat will result if the power steering gear is held in a full right or left turn for longer than a few seconds. This can result in damaged seals and/or pump.vicinityAUTHOR: ALAINA KEDANS6.9

content_text: 1GRANDE, WEST TRANSPORTATION 1VICINITY SERVICE MANUAL VERSION 1.0CHECKING SHOCK ABSORBERSFour hydraulic double acting shock absorbers are used on the suspension system: one at each front wheel, one adjacent to each rear air spring, and another on either side of the rear axle.The shock absorbers are sealed units with rubber brushed mountings and therefore require no servicing. However, they should still be checked and re-fitted for the following issues:· Visually inspect for fluid leakage.. Check for dents or cracks.· Check for scored or bent piston rod.· Check resistance by slowly expanding and contracting each shock absorber several times. Even resistance should be observed travelling in both directions.CHECKING HEIGHTThe rear suspension height is measured by calculating the distance from the bottom mounts to the top plates of the air spring assembly, located in front of the rear axle. This measurement should fall within the range of 230 mm ± 5 mm (9 in ± 0.2 in) for 27.5 ft buses, or 220 mm ± 5 mm (8.7 in ± 0.2 in) for 30 ft buses.CAUTION: It is imperative that the vehicle's suspension is to specification, particularly side-to-side deviations, so that vehicle dynamics are not disturbed.230 mm ± 5 mm27.5 ft buses only220 mm ± 5 mm30 ft buses onlyAUTHOR: ALAINA KEDANSvicinity7.2

content_text: GRANDE, WEST TRANSPORTATION 11VICINITY SERVICE MANUAL VERSION 1.0ECASOVERVIEWThis vehicle's suspension system comes equipped with a Meritor WABCO electronically controlled air suspension (ECAS) system, which is designed to enhance the performance of the air suspension. Its function is to maintain an accurate leveling of the chassis height through the use of level sensors, an electronic control unit (ECU), and solenoid valves. The ECAS system includes a customized set of parameters for this vehicle. These parameters determine some of the features and characteristics for the ECAS configuration.Two solenoid valve blocks, one located on the front suspension and one on the rear, control the air suspension on the vehicle.ELECTRONIC CONTROL UNITThe electronic control unit (ECU) is located within the interior electrical compartment of the vehicle. It connects to various other ECAS components and performs the following functions:. Monitors level and pressure sensors.· Controls solenoid valves.· Monitors function of system components, storing faults and performing diagnostics.WABCOWABCOCAUTION: Avoid damaging the ECU connectors when troubleshooting or testing the system.For further details on these operations, refer to the Meritor WABCO manual.INDICATOR LAMPThe ECAS indicator lamp, which is integrated into the LCD display panel standard on the instrument panel, indicates when ECAS system faults are detected by the electronic control unit (ECU). Faults are stored in its memory as active and when the fault clears, it will be stored as inactive. ECAS faults can be diagnosed using the Meritor WABCO TOOLBOX™ software. For more information on this software, refer to the Meritor WABCO manual.In the event of a system malfunction, the ECAS indicator lamp will alert the driver and the suspension will retain the existing air pressure in the air suspension bellows.For troubleshooting tips and diagnostic codes, refer to the Meritor WABCO manual.vicinityAUTHOR: ALAINA KEDANS7.4

content_text: 1GRANDE, WEST TRANSPORTATION 1VICINITY SERVICE MANUAL VERSION 1.0BRAKING SYSTEMDESCRIPTION! WARNINGOnly lift or move parts with a lifting device that has sufficient weight capacity. Ensure that the components are supported by suitable belts or hooks.Hub assembly weight: approx. 27 kg (60 lb) Brake disc weight: approx. 35 kg (77 lb) Caliper weight: approx. 45 kg (99 lb)The braking system is fully air operated with ABS, the front and rear service brakes being applied and released by the brake treadle during normal operation. It incorporates an emergency braking feature that utilizes parts of the rear service brake and parking brake systems, which is mechanically applied by spring brakes. These systems combine to stop the vehicle in the event of a brake system/air supply failure.This vehicle's braking system is in compliance with CMVSS 121.DISC BRAKESThe disc brakes encompass rotors, brake calipers/pads, and air actuators.See Front/Rear Disc Brake Sectioned View for a diagram of the parts listed in the next three sub- sections.BRAKE ACTUATIONDuring actuation, the Push Rod of the Actuator (18/1 or 18/2) moves the Lever (19). The input forces are transferred via the Eccentric Bearing (20) to the Bridge (17). The force is then distributed by the Bridge (17) and the two Threaded Tubes (16) to the Tappet and Boot Assemblies (13) and finally to the inboard Pad (12).After overcoming the running clearance between the Pads and the Disc, the reaction forces are transmitted to the outboard Pad (12). The clamping forces on the Pads (12) and the Disc (46) generate the braking force for the wheel.BRAKE RELEASEAfter releasing the air pressure, the two Return Springs (27/28) push the Bridge (17) and Lever (19) back to the start position; this ensures that a running clearance between Pads and Disc is maintained.BRAKE ADJUSTMENT (AUTOMATIC)To ensure a constant running clearance between Disc and Pads, the brake is equipped with a low wearing, automatic adjuster mechanism.The Adjuster (23
title: Vicinity Service Manual, p. 107

content_text: and Disc is maintained.BRAKE ADJUSTMENT (AUTOMATIC)To ensure a constant running clearance between Disc and Pads, the brake is equipped with a low wearing, automatic adjuster mechanism.The Adjuster (23) operates with every cycle of actuation due to the mechanical connection with Lever (19). As the Pads and Disc wear, the running clearance increases. The Adjuster (23) and Turning Device (24) turn the Threaded Tubes (16) by an amount necessary to compensate for this wear. The total running clearance (sum of clearance both sides of Disc) should be between 0.5 and 1.0 mm. smaller clearances may lead to overheating problems.AUTHOR: ALAINA KEDANSvicinity8.8

The valve has one park control, one service control, one supply, one balance, four delivery NPTF ports, and an exhaust port protected by an exhaust diaphragm.The valve incorporates two mounting studs for mounting the valve to the frame rail or cross member (where applicable).ABS/ATCWARNINGThe ATC function must be disabled (ATC indicator lamp should be ON) prior to performing any vehicle maintenance in which one or more wheels on an axle are lifted off the ground and moving.This vehicle's Bendix® Anti-lock Braking System (ABS) uses wheel speed sensors, ABS pressure modulator valves, and an Electronic Control Unit (ECU) to control all four wheels. The EC-60™ controller monitors individual wheel turning motion during braking, checking for excessive wheel slip or lock-up, and automatically adjusts the brake pressure accordingly at the wheel end.In addition to the ABS function, this vehicle's EC- 60™ controller also provides an Automatic Traction Control (ATC) feature. Similar to how ABS improves vehicle stability during braking, ATC improves vehicle stability and traction during vehicle acceleration. The ATC function uses the same wheel speed information and modulator control as the ABS function.For more information on these features, refer to the Bendix ABS manual.DIAGNOSTICSComputer-based Bendix® ACom® Diagnostics software can be utilized to access fault codes. For more information on interpreting trouble codes, refer to the Bendix ABS manual. Alternatively, there is a diagnostic switch that can be pressed to read the blink codes.Blink codes allow a technician to troubleshoot ABS problems without using a hand-held or PC-based diagnostic tool. When excessive wheel slip, or wheel lock-up, is detected, the EC-60™ controller will activate the PMV to simulate a brake application. The PMV are electro- pneumatic control valves and are the last valves that air passes through on its way to the brake chamber. content_text: 1GRANDE, WEST TRANSPORTATION 1VICINITY SERVICE MANUAL VERSION 1.0The main power for the vehicle is controlled by the battery disconnect switch, which is located in the rear of the engine compartment beside the power steering filter.RAPID CHECKTo quickly check the condition of a battery, turn on the vehicle lights and ignition. If the starter operates and the lights dim slightly, the battery is considered serviceable. However, if the lights fade drastically, this may be an indication that the battery is in a poor charge state and is incapable of supplying a strong current. It may also indicate that there is high resistance at the main connections between the posts and cable lugs.DISCHARGE TESTINGUse a high discharge tester to determine the battery is at least 70% charged.Optima battery should be tested as follows:. The discharge test should draw 1/2 of the rated C/C amps for 15 seconds with battery voltage staying above 9.6 Volts.Note: If the vehicle remains unused for a lengthy period of time, the battery will not maintain its charge.CORROSIONCAUTION: Excessive corrosion of the battery lugs will cause a voltage drop at the battery terminals, leading to sluggish operation of the starter.CAUTION: Allow batteries time to cool off after charging. Battery failure can possibly result if heat grows without cooling time, accelerating grid corrosion.Corroded battery lugs can be cleaned with petroleum jelly. Both the lugs and battery posts should be smeared with petroleum jelly or wax as a preventative measure against corrosion. If excessivecorrosion prevents a lug from being removed, wet a cloth with hot water and use it to twist off the corroded lug. After removing the corroded lug, proceed to remove all traces of corrosion.Note: Always keep the tops and terminals of batteries clean and free of corrosion. However, if they become hot to the touch, this could be an indication of a short. Discontinue the charging process and check the alternator immediately.When using an automatic charger to charge the batteries, let it run until it indicates that charging is complete.If using a manual charger, estimate total charging time for a completely discharged battery by multiplying the capacity (amp hours) by 1.2.Fully charged batteries should measure approximately 12.8V.Note: If purchasing a new battery charger, ensure that it has either AGM compatibility or a separate AGM charge setting. Minimal sensors are required as common sensor data (e.g. vehicle speed, engine temperature, etc.) are shared on the network. This allows for simplification of vehicle harnesses, reduction of fuse and relay usage, and increased diagnostic capability, thus reducing service time.MULTIPLEX NODESThe chassis and body nodes are the input/output modules. While they are identical in terms of hardware, their individual functions are determined by a master ladder logic program.MULTIPLEX MODULEWARNINGDo not start the module before the control system has been mounted and its electrical functions verified, or if anyone is near.CAUTION: Incorrectly positioned or mounted cabling can be influenced by radio signals, which can interfere with the functions of the system. The inputs are capable of being digital, frequency, or analog. The VMM1615 also includes two CAN communication ports that are used to communicate the status of multiple modules connected together in the same network.For more information on the VMM1615 multiplex module, including diagnostic LEDs, inputs and outputs, and CAN connections, refer to the Parker Vansco user guide.Vansco multiplexing module software and drivers are also available online for do

content_text: 1GRANDE, WEST TRANSPORTATION 1VICINITY SERVICE MANUAL VERSION 1.0CHAPTER 10 DOOR SYSTEMENTRANCE DOOROVERVIEWThis vehicle has an out-swing entrance door equipped with a Vapor rotary drive unit. The drive unit converts linear piston movements into rotary motion, which a spindle then transfers onto the door drive shaft. The single leaf door opens parallel to the outside curb side wall of the bus. For further information, refer to the Vapor Rotary Actuator guide.MECHANICAL COMPONENTSUsing a Vapor Pneumatic Rotary Operator, the entrance door opens outward in a circular motion parallel to the outside curb side wall of the bus.DOOR SHAFT ASSEMBLYThe door shaft is attached to the base of the rotary- drive unit by means of the boomerang assembly clamp. It pivots at the top of the bus structure using a maintenance free self-aligning bearing and bracket assembly.BOOMERANG ASSEMBLIESThe boomerang assemblies are connected to the door panel mounting brackets using self-aligning rod end bearings. Rubber stops are used to limit the opening movement of the door panel.GUIDE RODThe guide rod regulates the door panel's rotation on its hinge axis during opening and closing. It consists of two self-aligning rod end bearings threaded onto a connecting rod. The connecting rod assembly can be adjusted in length by rotating the rod. The rod length keeps the door panel parallel to the side ofthe vehicle in the door closed position and during door panel movement.DOOR PANELThis vehicle's high strength door panels incorporate furnishings for mounting door edges and seals.DOOR SEALS AND EDGESThe door panel is surrounded on all sides by weather resistant seals. An elastomeric rubber edge can be fitted to the hard edge of the door. If the door encounters an obstruction when attempting to close, the movement can be reversed by connecting a sealed edge to a pneumatic pressure wave switch.PNEUMATIC COMPONENTSUsing a Vapor Pneumatic Rotary Operator, the entrance door opens outward in a circular motion

This converts linear piston movements into rotary motion, which a spindle then transfers onto the door drive shaft. The rotary drive unit is comprised of a double-action pneumatic cylinder and helical transmission system.FLOW CONTROL VALVESFlow control valves are used to adjust the door speed. content_text: GRANDE, WEST 1TRANSPORTATION 1VICINITY SERVICE MANUAL VERSION 1.0This system is equipped with a 4-way door control solenoid valve, which requires a continuous electrical signal to open the door and maintain that position. The valve returns to its normal closed state when the electrical signal ceases.SLOW START VALVEThe purpose of this valve is to eliminate the slamming effect encountered during initial door system start up. It monitors the flow of air to the door operator until approximately 50% of system operating pressure is attained and then shifts to an unrestricted flow mode. By disallowing full air flow to the closing port until approximately 50% of system pressure is reached, the slow start valve prevents the door from slamming shut and potentially causing injury or damage.EMERGENCY VALVEThe emergency valve is a three-way valve that enables manual opening of the entrance door by exhausting air from the door system. Its design prevents a direct connection between the air supply port and the exhaust port at any position of the valve operating handle.When checking the functionality of the emergency valve for maintenance purposes, note that when it is actuated, it should be possible to open the door by using hand pressure to push it outward after approximately 5 seconds.ADJUSTMENT AND ALIGNMENTPRELOADINGWARNINGFailure to properly preload the door system could result in door seals pulling away from portal seals while the vehicle is moving.Preloading is a necessary step to ensure that the door is securely closed and sealed. This process involves elastically loading the door panel and shaft- and-arm assembly in the closed position. To preload the door system:1. Rotate the rotary output shaft and shaft- and-arm assembly clockwise (or counterclockwise for left handed units) until the cam follower rollers slide into the cam slot helical section.2. Insert a 9.9 mm (0.4 in) diameter pin gage in between the axial portion of the cam slots and the cam follower roller.3. Rot
title: Vicinity Service Manual, p. 134

content_text: s) until the cam follower rollers slide into the cam slot helical section.2. Insert a 9.9 mm (0.4 in) diameter pin gage in between the axial portion of the cam slots and the cam follower roller.3. Rotate the shaft-and-arm assembly counterclockwise until the round gage is lodged between the cam follower roller and the uppermost surface of the cam slot, creating a gap at the top and bottom of the door panel between the door and jam seals.4. Loosen the three socket head screws on the upper boomerang assembly. Rotate the upper boomerang arm counterclockwise to compress the door and jam seals against each other at the top of the door opening. Secure the upper boomerang to the shaft by holding the upper boomerang assembly and tightening the three socket head screws of the upper boomerang using 80 Nm (59 lb-ft) of torque to secure the upper boomerang to the shaft.5. Repeat Step #4 on the lower boomerang assembly.6. Apply 620 kPa (90 psi) of air pressure to the rotary operator assembly, which is the minimum pressure expected to be countered during operating service. Check the following:. The cam follower rollers must reach the upper end of the axial cam slots in order to lock the rotary operator in door closed position.vicinityAUTHOR: ALAINA KEDANS10.2

content_text: GRANDE, WEST TRANSPORTATION 11VICINITY SERVICE MANUAL VERSION 1.0. The door seals must make even contact around the entire portal opening. Push outward on the door panel along the portal seals to check for adequate seal compression.Operate the door system under power at minimum operating pressure to verify that the system preloaded properly. Ensure that the Rotary Operator cam followers move all the way up into the axial portion of the cam slots to lock the rotary operator in the door closed position.FLOW CONTROL VALVESThe door speed can be adjusted by means of the flow control valves that meter the exhaust flow of the rotary operator at working system pressure of 620 to 827 kPa (90 to 120 psi).DOOR SPEEDWARNINGSpeed and cushion adjustment screws are not captive and may become projectiles if adjusted too far counter clockwise under air pressure.The door opening time should be 2 to 3 seconds, whereas the closing time should be 1.5 to 3 seconds. If either exceeds 5 seconds, the corresponding flow control valve needs to be cleaned or readjusted.To adjust the opening/closing speed:1. Loosen the jam nut that secures the door close speed adjustment screw, which is located on the door engine end cap.2. Turn the screw counterclockwise to increase speed and clockwise to decrease speed.3. While securely holding the adjustment screw, tighten the jam nut to hold adjustment in place.CUSHIONINGWARNINGSpeed and cushion adjustment screws are not captive and may become projectiles if adjusted too far counter clockwise under air pressure.A piston cushioning device installed in the rotary drive allows for smooth opening of doors. It also reduces the impact of the door mechanism when it fully closes.The opening and closing cushion can be adjusted by means of the adjustment screws, which are located on the rotary drive unit. Turning these screws clockwise will increase the amount of cushioning. Turning them counterclockwise decreases the cushioning.SLOW START VALVEWARNINGDoor control sw

Closing the door cuts off the voltage supply to the solenoid valve.Adjusting the slow start valve is a more involved process than the other pneumatic system adjustments. To perform this adjustment, complete the following steps:1. With the emergency valve in the exhaust position, turn both adjustment screws on the slow start valve clockwise until they are lightly seated.2. Turn the adjustment screw designated "SPEED" counterclockwise at least four turns and secure into position with a jam nut.vicinityAUTHOR: ALAINA KEDANS10.3

content_text: GRANDE, WEST 1TRANSPORTATION 1VICINITY SERVICE MANUAL VERSION 1.0EXIT DOORDESCRIPTIONThe exit door system is comprised of a pneumatic rotary actuator, shaft assembly, and door panel assembly. A double acting cylinder drives a splined shaft through a helical ball cage to provide rotary motion. When the door reaches closed position, the actuator lifts the door shaft and door panel approximately 10 mm (0.4 in), which enables the door panel latches to connect the mating wedges on the door jams. The door panel will remain closed provided that air pressure is continuously being supplied to the actuator. The exit door panel also has a safety feature that allows the door panel to lift and reverse to an open position if a passenger or object obstructs the door while it is closing.SPECIFICATIONSMax. torque (locked position) . .. . 165 Nm (122 lb-ft) Operating temperature . . . - 30 to 80°℃ (-22 to 176°F) Operating pressure . . . . . 621 - 868 kPa (90 - 125 psi) Door opening/closing time 3 to 5 seconds Min. life cycle 500,000TROUBLESHOOTINGThe following troubleshooting methods can be carried out easily to fix common system malfunctions:· Door does not open/close.o There could be a shortage in the main power supply.o The 3-way valve might be closed. Rotate the 3-way valve handle to open the valve.· Noise is emitted when door panel opens.o The shaft might not be in alignment with the cylinder shaft.Loosen the operator mounting screws, then open and close the door manually. Tighten the loosened screws when the noise ceases.· Operator works, but without cushioning.o Adjust the cushion screw until the door operates with cushioning. If the speed is too high, adjust speed control.MAINTENANCEThe door panel is made of high strength alloy aluminum and designed to be long-lasting. It is therefore a non-serviceable item. However, the following checks should be performed on the exit door system:· Test the emergency valve function.o Note that when the emergency valve function is actuated, i

The door panel will then drop, enabling the door panel to be manually opened.. Test the exit door safety feature function.· Ensure that the voltage of the power supply and solenoid valve are the same.. Ensure that the door panel lifts smoothly.. Ensure that when the door closes, the actuator lifts the door shaft and door panel at least 10 mm (0.4 in).. content_text: GRANDE, WEST 1TRANSPORTATION 1VICINITY SERVICE MANUAL VERSION 1.0CHAPTER 12 HVACHEATING SYSTEMAUXILIARY HEATERWARNINGThe auxiliary heater must be switched off to prevent explosions where flammable fumes or dust may build up (e.g. when in the vicinity of fuel, coal, wood, cereal depots, or similar installations).WARNINGDue to the danger of poisoning and suffocation the auxiliary heater must not be operated, not even with timed operation, in enclosed areas that are not equipped with an exhaust venting.WARNINGDue to the danger of poisoning and suffocation the auxiliary heater must not be operated, not even with timed operation, in enclosed areas that are not equipped with an exhaust venting.This vehicle's Spheros auxiliary heater is used to heat the passenger compartment, defrost the windshield, and preheat the engine. The auxiliary heater operates independently from the engine. It is connected to the cooling system, fuel system, and electrical system. Its components include a combustion air fan, fuel pump, heat exchanger, combustion chamber, and electronic ignition coil.The auxiliary heater can be turned on by activating the auxiliary heater switch on the left front dash ofthe driver's station. content_text: GRANDE, WEST TRANSPORTATION 11VICINITY SERVICE MANUAL VERSION 1.0CHAPTER 13 WINDSHIELDWIPER SYSTEMDESCRIPTIONThis vehicle has a one-piece windshield that spans the width of the bus. The windshield size is 1473 by 2667 mm (58 by 105 in). It is equipped with an electrically controlled two-speed, dual-blade windshield wiper system.The windshield wipers are controlled by a rotary switch on the left front dash of the driver's station. The switch has four positions: off, intermittent, low, and high. Rotate switch to intermittent to engage the windshield wipers once every 7 seconds.IntermittentLowOffHighIIThis vehicle's wiper system is in compliance with CMVSS 104 Windshield Wiping and Washing System.MAINTENANCEThe windshield wiper blades should be inspected and lubricated regularly. Replace them when they wear out.PREVENTATIVE MAINTENANCERegardless of weather conditions, the windshield wiper system should be operated at least once per day. This promotes sufficient lubrication and prevents rapid wear of components.WIPER ARM REPLACEMENT! WARNINGIsolate the wiper system before performing maintenance in the area to avoid personal injury due to entrapment of moving parts.Complete the following steps to remove and mount the wiper arms:1. Park the wiper system by switching the wipers on and then off. After turning off, the wiper motor should continue to run until it returns to the "park" position.2. Remove the wiper motor from the vehicle harness.3. Remove and set aside the wiper arms and blades. The wiper arms can be safely removed using a 2-jaw puller.4. Remove the wiper arm head splines with a file, ensuring to maintain taper shape.5. Beginning on the road side, assemble the wiper arm to the pivot and position the blade horizontally. Angle the blade up 2° and tighten the pivot nut using a torque of 40 Nm ± 5 Nm.6. Assemble the curb side wiper arm to the pivot and position the blade horizontally. Angle the blade up 1° and tighten the pivot nut using a torque of 40 Nm + 5 Nm.7.

content_text: 1GRANDE, WEST TRANSPORTATION 1VICINITY SERVICE MANUAL VERSION 1.0ALIGNMENTROAD SIDEWhen aligning the road side wipers, ensure that the motor crank and connecting rod are in a straight line. If required, the motor crank can be removed and torqued to 22 - 27 Nm (16 - 20 lb-ft). The angle between the pivot crank and connecting rod should be 44° + 2°. If the angle falls outside of this range, the connecting rod length can be adjusted by loosening the bolts and sliding to desired position. Tighten bolts to a torque of 23 - 25 Nm (17 - 18 lb- ft).Connecting rodMotor crankCorrect alignmentConnecting rodMotor crankIncorrect alignmentCURB SIDEWhen aligning the curb side wipers, ensure that the delay centre and connecting rod are in a straight line. If required, loosen delay adjustment bolts and slide to the desired position. Tighten bolts to a torque of 23 - 25 Nm (17 - 18 lb-ft). The angle between the pivot crank and connecting rod should be 42° + 2°. If the angle falls outside of this range, the connecting rod length can be adjusted by loosening the bolts and sliding to desired position. Then, tighten bolts to a torque of 23 - 25 Nm (17 - 18 lb-ft).ADJUSTMENTThe curb side wiper can be adjusted to avoid over- sweeping as follows:1. Remove wiper arm using a 2-jaw puller.2. Adjust curb side connecting rod to a length of 627mm (24.7 in). Torque bolts to 23 - 25 Nm (17 - 18 lb-ft).3. Adjust the delay connecting rod to align in a straight line, as shown in the adjustment diagram. Torque bolts to 23 - 25 Nm (17 - 18 lb-ft).4. Remount the wiper arm and torque to 40 Nm ± 5 Nm (26 to 33 lb-ft). Clean splines if necessary.vicinityAUTHOR: ALAINA KEDANS13.2

content_text: GRANDE, WEST TRANSPORTATION 11VICINITY SERVICE MANUAL VERSION 1.0CHAPTER 2 MAINTENANCEDAILY MAINTENANCE CHECKSCHECKING ENGINE OIL LEVELThe engine oil dipstick can be accessed from the curb side rear engine door.Engine oil dipstickIn order to check the oil level:1. Shut off the engine for an accurate reading.2. Wait at least 15 minutes after shutting off the engine to check the oil level. This allows time for the oil to drain into the oil pan.Use oil grade API CG-4/SL ACEA E5 15W/40 CES 20077.CAUTION: Never operate the engine if the oil level is below the low (L) mark or above the high (H) mark as this can result in engine damage or poor engine performance.@Cumming/IncHHOKLL0190045CHECKING COOLANT LEVEL! WARNINGDo not remove a pressure cap from a hot engine. Wait until the coolant temperature is below 50℃ (120°F) before removing the pressure cap.The coolant level is displayed on the expansion tank, which can be accessed from behind the rear engine door.CAUTION: Never use a sealing additive to stop leaks in the cooling system. This can result in cooling system plugging and inadequate coolant flow, causing the engine to overheat.ENGINE COOLANT ONLYHEATING LOOP COOLANT ONLYFULL HOTFULL COLDFULLCummins Inc. recommends the use of fully formulated antifreeze/coolant meeting Cummins Engineering Standards (C.E.S.) 14603.vicinityAUTHOR: ALAINA KEDANS2.1

content_text: GRANDE, WEST TRANSPORTATION 11VICINITY SERVICE MANUAL VERSION 1.0CHECKING TRANSMISSION OIL LEVEL! WARNINGInsufficient oil in the system can lead to partial or complete failure of the retarder, rendering braking action impaired or unavailable.Transmission oil level should be checked once every 10,000 km. The transmission oil dipstick can be accessed from the rear engine compartment door.CAUTION: Always maintain the correct oil level as insufficient oil can lead to transmission malfunction and damage. Too much oil will cause the transmission to overheat.Oil filler tubeSteps for checking the transmission oil level are listed as follows:1. Confirm that the oil level is at operating temperature (between 80℃ and 90℃) in order to obtain a definitive reading.2. Ensure vehicle is stationary and on level ground.3. Shift range selector (pushbutton) to Neutral position.4. Run engine for 15 to 20 seconds at 1200 - 1500 rpm (not required with directly mounted heat exchanger).5. Let engine run at idle speed (500 - 700 rpm). The speed must never drop below 450 rpm.CAUTION: Idle speed should be set between 500 and 700 rpm. It must never drop below 400 rpm as this will cause the engine to stall.Follow up with regular visual inspection of the transmission for signs of leakage. In exceptional cases the oil level may need to be checked while the transmission oil is cold, then checked again at normal operating temperature.For further instructions, refer to the ZF-EcoLife or ZF- Ecomat 4 manual.CHECKING POWER STEERING FLUIDThe power steering fluid reservoir is located in the engine compartment and can be accessed from the rear engine door.06/05/2015The fluid level should be checked with the engine at idle and maintained at the max level indicator.Recommended fluid: Automatic Transmission Fluid Dexron IIIvicinityAUTHOR: ALAINA KEDANS2.2

content_text: 1GRANDE, WEST TRANSPORTATION 1VICINITY SERVICE MANUAL VERSION 1.0TOWING AND LIFTING! WARNINGFailure to comply with the safety precautions in this section could result in personal injury or vehicle damage. Always follow the recommended procedures. The operator of the towing vehicle is ultimately responsible for safely securing and towing the vehicle. Ensure that the operator of the towing vehicle is aware of the safety requirements and towing procedures contained in this section.! WARNINGFollow all government safety regulations. A vehicle safety restraint system must be used that is independent of the primary lifting and towing attachments.TOWINGCAUTION: Before towing the vehicle, the transmission must be shifted into Neutral. Failure to do so will cause damage to the drive shaft or rear axles.Without a means of supplying air to the vehicle being towed, the parking brake (spring brake) must be released. Please refer to the rear braking section for information on this process.An air coupling to supply air to the vehicle is available within the front road side access panel. It is recommended that a ramp truck only be used when towing the Vicinity Bus. If a ramp style truck is not available, then the Vicinity bus must be towed using the tow eyes on the front of the bus.1Air couplingCare must be taken to ensure that the vehicle will not suffer structural or drivetrain damage as a result of towing.CAUTION: The driveshaft or both rear axle shafts must be removed when towing, regardless of distance or speed traveled. Damage to the transmission/drive unit may occur if the vehicle is towed without first removing the driveshaft or rear axles.vicinityAUTHOR: ALAINA KEDANS2.5

content_text: 1GRANDE, WEST TRANSPORTATION 1VICINITY SERVICE MANUAL VERSION 1.0LIFTINGWARNINGDo not walk under a vehicle being lifted until the lifts are stopped and in a "locked" position and/or jack stands are positioned under the chassis.WARNINGThe axles must not hang unsupported on the shock absorbers as this could result in serious injury or death. Always follow the proper lifting procedures provided by the Hoist or Lift manufacturer's operating instructions.When lifting the vehicle for maintenance, always hoist at the front wheel and drive wheel or designated chassis locations. Chassis distortion and/or body damage can occur if lifting is attempted at points not designated. We strongly recommend that wheel lifts are used and remain in place for support.After hoisting the bus to working height, place additional jack stands under the axles for support.Position lift equipment and jack stands on a firm and level surface. content_text: GRANDE, WEST TRANSPORTATION 11VICINITY SERVICE MANUAL VERSION 1.0STARTING SYSTEMOVERVIEWThe 24V starting system is comprised of a starting motor, starter solenoid, integral magnetic switch relay, starter switches, circuit breakers, and electrical connections. The integral magnetic switch relay minimizes voltage drops and allows the solenoid to receive the maximum voltage available in any starting condition.ROTATION CHECKIf the starter solenoid is making noise, but the engine is not rotating, the starting motor may need to be replaced. To determine this, perform a rotation check:1. Make note of the starting motor voltage before beginning cranking.2. Turn the ignition to the OFF position and attempt to bar the crankshaft in both directions.3. Use a Cummins-approved barring tool to bar the engine.· If the crankshaft bars over, attempt to start the engine. If the starter motor cranks the engine, the issue may be damage to the starter motor pinion gear and flywheel ring gear.. If the crankshaft does not rotate or requires more than the normal effort to bar, there may be either an internal malfunction or a problem with the drive unit and/or accessories.4. 1. If the engine cranking speed is slower than usual or does not crank and the engine rotates freely:. Ensure that the wiring connections are clean, tight, and undamaged.· Check the battery voltage.5. If the voltage drops more than 4.8-VDC during the rotation check, ensure that all electrical connections are clean and tight. If the cables are correct and the voltage continues to drop below the limit, replace the starting motor.MAINTENANCE! WARNINGBatteries can emit explosive gases. To reduce the possibility of personal injury, always ventilate the compartment before servicing the batteries. Remove the negative (-) battery cable first and attach the negative (-) battery cable last.! WARNINGHot steam can cause serious bodily harm. Wear safety glasses or a face shield and protective clothing when using a steam cleaner.! WAR

If equipped with a starting motor spacer, remove the spacer and clean all surfaces between the starting motor, starting motor spacer, and flywheel housing with a wire brush.4. Clean any leftover sealant from the starting motor mounting flange on both the wet flywheel housing (if applicable) and starting motor. Ensure that these components are clean of oil and debris.5. Re-install all removed parts and the new starting motor per the Cummins manual installation instructions.6. Connect the electrical connection to the starting motor.7. Connect the batteries. Operate the starting motor to ensure proper function.CAUTION: Do not overtighten the electrical connections as starter damage can result.COOLING SYSTEMDESCRIPTIONThe cooling system is comprised of an engine driven water pump, thermostat, radiator, and electric cooling fans.When the engine starts, the engine belt turns a water pump that pushes coolant through the engine block. A thermostat is used to control the flow of coolant, providing efficient engine warm-up and regulating coolant temperature. When the coolant temperature falls below the operating range, engine coolant is bypassed back to the inlet of the water pump. When the engine coolant temperature reaches the operating range (86℃), the thermostat opens, seals off the bypass, thus forcing the coolant to flow to the radiator. Warm coolant enters the top of the radiator, flows out the bottom, and enters the transmission oil cooler. It then flows through the heat exchanger and returns back to the engine where the temperature is regulated and the process repeats once it heats up again.The six cooling fans are controlled by sensors placed in the radiator coolant flow. The variable speed fans are controlled by the TMC control unit.SPECIFICATIONSCoolant type Cummins Standard 14603 Capacity 70 litres (18.5 gallons)Min. coolant strength50% water/50% a

content_text: GRANDE, WEST 1TRANSPORTATION 1VICINITY SERVICE MANUAL VERSION 1.0COOLANT LOW LEVEL INDICATORWhen the coolant level falls below a predetermined level, the CHECK ENGINE lamp, controlled by the engine control module (ECM), will flash for 30 seconds.CAUTION: Low coolant level is not always indicative of a leak in the cooling system. However, the cooling system should be checked for leaks and repaired, if necessary, as soon as the lamp comes on.COOLANT HOSESRadiator hoses are used to direct coolant between the engine and the radiator. The upper radiator hose connects the thermostat housing to the radiator inlet. The lower radiator hose connects the radiator to the water pump inlet.Coolant hoses should be regularly checked for signs of deterioration. Hardened, cracked, swollen, or restricted hoses should be replaced. If a hose shows any signs of chafing, the cause should be fixed immediately.Note: The silicone engine coolant hose will exhibit swelling due to the elasticity of the hose. This is normal behaviour and does not require replacing.PRESSURE TESTING!
