content_text:
Flowchart titled "Troubleshoot High Coolant Temperature" outlining stepwise diagnostic checks and corrective actions:

- Start: Check whether fault codes other than 07‑NN are present. If yes, go to "Troubleshoot Other Fault Codes."
- If no, proceed through a sequence of physical checks and fixes:
  - Inspect air flow path for obstructions; if fail, remove obstructions.
  - Check coolant level; if low, adjust coolant level.
  - Check coolant mixture; if incorrect, adjust mixture.
  - Check that the cooling system is deaerated; if not, deaerate.
  - Inspect fans; if fan fails inspection, replace fan.
  - Inspect recirculation prevention; if failing, correct recirculation prevention.
  - After each successful step, continue to the next check until completion of this left-hand branch.
- Parallel/right branch focused on heat exchanger, fans, thermostat, and sensors:
  - Inspect heat exchanger for cleanliness; if dirty, clean heat exchanger.
  - Test maximum fan performance; if fan is slow or not operating, troubleshoot fan operation.
  - Test thermostat operation; if failing, replace thermostat.
  - Perform test drive; if pass, troubleshooting is done.
  - If test drive fails, determine which coolant sensor is used (engine sensor vs cooling system sensor) and compare coolant measurements between the sensors.
    - If the comparison fails (measurements inconsistent), troubleshoot incorrect coolant temperature.
    - If the comparison passes, contact EMP support.
- End conditions: either "Done" after a passing test drive or escalation to sensor troubleshooting/EMP support if issues persist.
title: 20180131200843 emp-cooling-fans-service-manual, p. 104

  - If No → proceed to thermostat test.
- Step: "Test Thermostat Operation."
  - If Fail → "Replace Thermostat."
  - If Pass → proceed.
- Step: "Determine Coolant Sensor Used" with two sensor branches:
  - Cooling system sensor branch:
    - "Compare Coolant Measurements."
      - If Fail → "Troubleshoot Incorrect Coolant Temperature."
      - If Pass → "Contact EMP Support."
  - Engine sensor branch:
    - "Verify J1939 Coolant Temperature Received."
      - If Pass → "Contact EMP Support."
      - If Fail → "Check Engine Communication."
        - If Fail → "Troubleshoot Vehicle J1939 Connection."
        - If Pass → "Contact EMP Support."

Each decision routes to either a remedial action or the next diagnostic step; final resolution options include replacing the thermostat, troubleshooting communications (EMP‑Link or J1939), troubleshooting incorrect coolant temperature measurement, or contacting EMP support.

Flowchart for troubleshooting high intake air temperature:

- First decision: are fault codes other than 07-NN present?
  - Yes → troubleshoot those other fault codes.

- Sequential inspections (each step: if Fail → perform the listed corrective action; if Pass → continue):

  2. Inspect intake air for leaks. Fail → repair intake air leaks.

content_text:
Flowchart for troubleshooting a slow or non‑operating fan with two parallel paths: fault‑code checks and hardware checks.

Left branch — fault codes and basic fan checks:
- Start: "Troubleshoot Fan Slow Or Not Operating".
- Decision: "Is Fault Code 03‑NN Active?" — Yes → "Troubleshoot Fault Code 03‑NN"; No → next decision.
- Decision: "Is Fault Code 04‑NN Active?" — Yes → "Troubleshoot Fault Code 04‑NN"; No → "Check Fan Operation".
- From "Check Fan Operation":
  - If Pass → "Test Maximum Fan Performance".
    - If Pass → "Clear Fault Code" → proceed to the hardware inspection sequence (right column).
    - If Fail → follow the fail path (see below).
  - If Fail → verify obstruction and airflow:
    - "Verify Fan Is Not Obstructed" — if Fail → "Remove Fan Obstruction".
    - After verifying fan, "Inspect Air Flow Path For Obstructions" — if Fail → "Remove Air Flow Obstructions".
  - The fail conditions feed back into the testing/verification loop until resolved.

Right branch — FIL‑11 fan hardware and power checks:
- "Inspect FIL‑11 Fan Connector":
  - If Fail → "Repair FIL‑11 Fan Connector".
  - If Pass → "Check FIL‑11 Power Voltage".
    - If Power check Pass → "Replace FIL‑11 Fan".
    - If Power check Fail (High) → "Troubleshoot High Voltage".
    - If Power check Fail (Low or Zero) → "Troubleshoot FIL‑11 Power".

Overall, the diagram routes from fault‑code diagnostics to functional testing, obstruction removal, connector inspection, power‑voltage checks, and ultimately fan replacement or specific repairs based on the failing condition.

Flowchart titled "Troubleshoot Fan Runs When Ignition Off" with these steps and decision points:

- Start: "Is Engine Running?" (decision)
  - Yes → "Determine If Engine Shutdown Is Required" (action)

  - Fail → "Troubleshoot System Wakeup" (action/end of that branch).

- "Check System Wakeup Not Shorted To Power"
  - Pass → "Contact EMP Support" (action/end).
  - Fail → "Inspect FiL-11 Connector (All Fans)" (action).

- "Inspect FiL-11 Connector (All Fans)"
  - Fail → "Repair FiL-11 Connector" (action).
  - Pass → "Inspect TMC Grey 12 Pin Connector" (action).

- "Inspect TMC Grey 12 Pin Connector"
  - Fail → "Repair TMC Grey 12 Pin Connector" (action).
  - Pass → "Replace Main Harness" (action/end).

The flow loops from the "Determine If Engine Shutdown Is Required" No outcome and from the initial "Is Engine Running?" No outcome into the "Check System Wakeup Voltage" step.

Flowchart titled "Troubleshoot LED Not Functioning" that begins with the decision "Is the LED On or Off?"

- If Off:

    - Pass → Test LED Operation
      - Pass → Done (end)
      - Fail → Verify LED Polarity
        - Fail → Correct LED Polarity (end)
        - Pass → Inspect Pushbutton LED Connector
          - Fail → Repair Pushbutton LED Connector (end)
          - Pass → Inspect TMC Black 12‑Pin Connector
            - Fail → Repair TMC Black 12‑Pin Connector (end)
            - Pass → proceed to the right‑hand test sequence

- If On:
  - proceed directly to the right‑hand test sequence

Right‑hand test sequence (entered from either branch):
- Test LED Socket Voltage
  - Pass → Replace LED (end)
  - Fail → Check Main Harness LED Voltage
    - Pass → Replace Pushbutton LED Harness (end)
    - Fail → Test TMC LED Output
      - Pass → Replace Main Harness (end)
      - Fail → Replace TMC (end)

The flowchart specifies pass/fail branching at each test and corresponding corrective actions or next tests.

- Step 1: "Check Fault Status Information".
  - If result is "No Concern" → action: "Clear Fault Code".
  - If result indicates a "Possible Issue" → proceed to Step 2.
- Step 2: "Check TMC Power Voltage".
  - If the check "Pass" → action: "Replace TMC".
  - If the check shows "Fail High" → action: "Troubleshoot High Voltage".
title: 20180131200843 emp-cooling-fans-service-manual, p. 43

content_text:
Flowchart for troubleshooting Fault Code 02-02:

- Start: "Troubleshoot Fault Code 02-02".
- Step 1: Check fault status information.
  - If "No Concern": clear the fault code (end).
  - If "Possible Issue": proceed.
- Step 2: Check battery voltage.
  - If battery voltage fails/low: troubleshoot low voltage (end).
  - If battery voltage passes: proceed.
- Step 3: Check TMC power voltage.
  - If TMC power voltage passes: replace the TMC (end).
  - If TMC power voltage fails: inspect TMC power pins.
    - If inspection fails: repair TMC power pins (end).
    - If inspection passes: replace main harness (end).
title: 20180131200843 emp-cooling-fans-service-manual, p. 45

content_text:
Flowchart for troubleshooting Fault Code 02‑03:

- Start: "Troubleshoot Fault Code 02‑03".
- Step 1: Inspect system wakeup connector.
  - If Fail → Repair system wakeup connector.
  - If Pass → proceed.
- Step 2: Check system wakeup voltage.
  - If Fail → Troubleshoot system wakeup.
  - If Pass → proceed.
- Step 3: Inspect TMC ignition enable pin.
  - If Fail → Repair TMC ignition enable pin.
  - If Pass → proceed.
- Step 4: Check TMC wakeup voltage.
  - If Fail (low) → Replace main harness.
  - If Pass → Replace TMC.
title: 20180131200843 emp-cooling-fans-service-manual, p. 47

content_text:
Flowchart for troubleshooting Fault Code 03-NN and associated FiL-11 fan issues:

- Start: "Troubleshoot Fault Code 03-NN".
- Decision: "Are All Fault Codes 03-NN Active?"
  - Yes → "Troubleshoot TMC EMP-Link #1 Communication".
  - No → next decision.
- Decision: "Is Fault Code 04-NN Active?"
  - Yes → "Troubleshoot Fault Code 04-NN".
  - No → proceed to physical inspections.
- Action: "Inspect FiL-11 Fan Power Pins"
  - If Fail → "Repair FiL-11 Power Pins".
  - If Pass → continue.
- Action: "Inspect FiL-11 Fan EMP-Link Pins"
  - If Fail → "Repair FiL-11 EMP-Link Pins".
  - If Pass → continue.
- Action: "Check FiL-11 Fan Operation"
  - If Pass → "Troubleshoot FiL-11 Fan Communication".
  - If Fail → continue.
- Action: "Check FiL-11 Fan Power Voltage"
  - If Fail → "Troubleshoot FiL-11 Fan Power".
  - If Pass → "Troubleshoot FiL-11 Fan Wakeup".

Arrows indicate the sequential flow and conditional branching (Yes/No or Pass/Fail) between decisions, inspections, repairs, and troubleshooting subroutines.

content_text: 3 LIONRepair Procedure: Replacement of the Steering BoxPROCED. #:RP-01-34-00-00-004Publication Date:2022-09-08Page 2 of 8SAFETY PRECAUTIONSWhen working on the vehicle, make sure the starter switch is in the "OFF" position, the parking brake is set, and the tires are chocked. Before working under the vehicle, always place jack stands under the frame rails to ensure the vehicle cannot drop. Failure to follow these steps can cause serious injuries or death.Tools used when working near batteries or electrical connections must be certified to a rating of 1000 Vdc to prevent injuries from electric shock. Short circuits between components or wires must be avoided.MAINTENANCE REFERENCEThis procedure is done in conjunction with MP-01-34-00-00-001 Drag Link Inspection.DURATIONThe duration of the repair procedure is approximately 90 minutes.LIST OF MATERIAL· Steering box hydraulic P/N 15301060TOOLS· Appropriate wrench· Certified and calibrated torque wrench· Container· Ratchet with appropriate sockets

Reconnect the two hydraulic lines with the fitting hand tight plus two more turns.16. Before connecting the steering shaft, verify the position of the flat spot on the steering box gear (Figure 6). A bolt will be inserted through the hole in the gear.H5G313Figure 6 - Flat Spot on the Steering Box Gear17. Reconnect the steering shaft with the gear of the steering box Make sure that the hole on the steering shaft is aligned with the one on the steering box.18. Install a new bolt through the steering shaft and the gear of the steering box (Figure 2).19. Install a new nut on the bolt and torque it to 75.2 ft-lb (102 Nm).20. content_text: D LIONRepair Procedure: Replacement of the Steering BoxPROCED. #:RP-01-34-00-00-004Publication Date:2022-09-08Page 7 of 8PROCEDURE (Continued)!Warning Do not allow the fluid level to drop significantly or run out of the reservoir. This may induce air into the reservoir.22. Turn the starter switch to "START" for 10 seconds to activate the hydraulic system. Then turn the switch to "OFF".23. Verify the fluid level in the reservoir. If necessary, add some fluid.24. Repeat the process at least three times.25. Turn the starter switch to "START".26. Turn the steering wheel completely from left to right with a 2-second hold when reached. Repeat a few times.27. Make sure the front wheels turn in the same direction as the steering wheel with minimum resistance and no hydraulic leaks from the two fitting elbows are apparent.28. Add fluid as necessary.29. Centered the steering wheel.30. Loosen the manual bleed screw one turn on the steering box (Figure 7).

content_text:
Technical assembly drawing showing multiple orthogonal views (top, front, side, rear, bottom) of a cylindrical burner/heat-exchanger unit with labeled components, connection points, mounting features, and key dimensions (in inches with millimeters in brackets).

Main components and connections:
- Cylindrical housing containing a heat exchanger and burner head; exhaust outlet and inlet labeled on the side/top views.
- Fuel connection: JIC male fuel inlet with internal fuel filter shown on the side view.
- Temperature sensors: T1 primary temperature sensor location indicated; T2 secondary temperature sensor location noted (sensor not shown).
- Air intake and an alternate snorkel intake option referenced; snorkel hose requirement noted in the notes.
- Exhaust location and recommended exhaust cutout/pipe requirements referenced.
- Heat exchanger identified on the rear/side views.

Mounting and service features:
- Four M8 x 1.25 mounting PEM nuts on the end face; six 0.41 in (10 mm) holes shown on the bottom view.
- Service space requirement called out for removal of burner head and combustion tube for inspection/cleaning.

Key dimensions (selected):
- Overall length approx. 23.24 in (590 mm).
- Body/face diameters and widths shown; example rear-face width 10.13 in (257 mm) and 9.00 in (229 mm) in one view.
- Several centerline offsets and local distances identified (examples: 12.60 in/320 mm between specific features; 9.55 in/243 mm from inlet bracket to a reference).

Notes summary (referenced on drawing):
- Dimensions are in inches (millimeters in brackets).
- Typical exhaust cutout 3.25 in centered on exhaust.
- Exhaust pipe recommendations: minimum diameter 2.75 in, maximum length 5 ft, no more than 180° of bends.
- Alternate fuel inlet and heat exchanger configurations available; snorkel and inlet/outlet reversal require additional parts or sensor (T2) per notes.

Overall, the drawing provides dimensional data, sensor and connection placements, mounting hole patterns, and service/installation constraints for the burner/heat-exchanger assembly.
title: ProHeat service manual m50 m80 sl9150, p. 15

content_text:
A wiring and connector diagram for the PROHEAT G‑I PCM showing the PCM housing and its multi‑pin connectors plus the complete pin‑to‑function wiring between the PROHEAT module and the OEM harness.

Key elements and connections
- PCM connector layout: the module has multiple external connectors identified P1 through P6 (plus temperature sensor connectors). P1 = Power, P2 = Control (switch/interface), P3 = Datalink/download (RS‑232), P4 = Pump (coolant), P5 = Auxiliary (output), P6 = CAN bus (optional). Additional small connectors labeled for T1/T2 temperature sensors.
- Power feed and protection: battery positive feeds the PCM power input through a 30 A fuse to the PCM power supply; battery negative is vehicle ground.
- Control and outputs (P2, P4, P5):
  - P2 (Control) provides: indicator output (high‑side switched), indicator ground, constant power output (timer/switch remote panel), accessory ground, main switch input (ON signal / preheat unlatch), preheat switch input, supplemental switch input, and pump/coolant switch input.
  - P4 (Pump) provides the coolant pump output and pump ground (pump circuit shown rated up to a 10 A maximum).
  - P5 (Auxiliary) provides an auxiliary high‑side switched output and its ground.
- Communications and diagnostics:
  - P3 (Datalink) provides RS‑232 RX/TX, ground, an indicator output, accessory power output, and a factory use pin (some pins noted as N/A).
  - P6 (CAN bus) provides CAN‑H, CAN‑L and shield conductors (optional).
- User interface and external controls:
  - An indicator lamp connection is shown (location per customer/OEM).
  - A timer option / remote control with four conductors (red, green, white, black) and a spring‑centered momentary toggle switch on the driver’s console is shown as an optional interface to the PCM.
  - A mechanics‑disable switch and an engine‑run (alternator) signal input are included to inhibit or allow heater/pump operation based on vehicle status.
- Current and signal limits: many control/indicator outputs are limited to 1 A max (noted on the diagram); pump/coolant output has a higher label (maximum 10 A shown); main feed is protected by a 30 A fuse.
- Connector and sealing notes: the diagram calls out Metri‑Pack connector series (power uses a larger Metri‑Pack series) and specifies that unused PCM connector positions are supplied with seal plugs. A parts table lists connector and seal part numbers.

Purpose
- The diagram documents pin assignments, required external connections (power, ground, switch inputs, communications, pump and auxiliary loads), and protection/limit requirements needed to integrate the PROHEAT G‑I PCM with an OEM wiring harness.
title: ProHeat service manual m50 m80 sl9150, p. 17

content_text:
Exploded assembly diagram of a compact combustion heater showing the main mechanical, fuel, ignition, and sensor components and how they connect:

- Overall layout: airflow and combustion components align axially from the blower at one end through the burner/combustion tube into a cylindrical heat exchanger, which has an inlet and an outlet for coolant/gases.
- Air path and drive: ambient air enters the blower housing through an air filter, is driven by the combustion air blower and motor, and is delivered to the burner head flange (which on some models includes a built‑in air compressor). A separate inset shows a rotary vane air compressor (serial numbers 600000–699999) and its air relief.
- Burner assembly and fuel system: the burner head flange contains the fuel supply pump, fuel regulator, fuel shut‑off valve, fuel nozzle, ignition module, and ignition electrodes. An inset provides a close‑up of these burner/fuel components.
- Combustion chamber: air and fuel mix and ignite in the combustion tube; combustion gases pass through the tube into the heat exchanger.
- Heat exchanger and sensors: the heat exchanger receives combustion gases at its inlet and discharges them at the outlet. Temperature Sensor 1 is mounted on the heat exchanger; an optional Temperature Sensor 2 (shown in a separate detail) is required for reverse coolant flow.
- Controls: the G‑I PCM (ProHeat control module) is shown mounted near the blower/motor assembly and interfaces with the ignition, fuel pump, and sensors.

The drawing emphasizes component relationships and assembly order rather than internal detail of each part.
title: ProHeat service manual m50 m80 sl9150, p. 24

content_text: 3 LIONRepair Procedure: BTMS Compressor ReplacementPROCED. #:RP-01-13-00-00-006Publication Date:2023-05-16Page 2 of 7SAFETY PRECAUTIONSWhen working on the vehicle, make sure the starter switch is in the "OFF" position, the parking brake is set, and the tires are chocked. Before working under the vehicle, always place jack stands under the frame rails to ensure the vehicle cannot drop. Failure to follow these steps can cause serious injuries or death.Tools used when working near batteries or electrical connections must be certified to a rating of 1000 Vdc to prevent injuries from electric shock. Short circuits between components or wires must be avoided.MAINTENANCE REFERENCEThis procedure is done each time the BTMS compressor needs to be replaced.DURATIONThe duration of the repair procedure is approximately 120 minutes.LIST OF MATERIAL· BTMS compressor P/N 11602566TOOLS· ACS machine· Combination wrench· Crow foot 3/8 drive socket· Calibrated and certified torque wrench. Clean container· Ratchet with appropriate sockets
title: RP-01-13-00-00-006 BTMS Compressor Replacement, p. 2

content_text: 1 LIONRepair Procedure: BTMS Compressor ReplacementPROCED. #:RP-01-13-00-00-006Publication Date: 2023-05-16Page 3 of 7CONSUMABLES· Freon R134a· PAG oil (SP-A2)PROCEDURE!Warning Only trained and certified technicians are allowed to perform any work on the refrigerant system.!CautionMake sure that all the local safety measure regarding the handling of an ACS machine is followed.1. Make sure that the work can be done safely.2. Make sure the vehicle is on a flat surface.3. Deactivate the high voltage as per MP-01-05-00-00-002 High-Voltage Circuit Deactivation Procedure for BMW Batteries.4. Locate the BTMS compressor (Figure 2).Figure 2 - Location of the BTMS Compressor5. Connect an ACS machine to the compressor and remove the refrigerant gas from the BTMS (Figure 3).
title: RP-01-13-00-00-006 BTMS Compressor Replacement, p. 3

Disconnect the two conduits that are connected to the compressor (Figure 4).Figure 4 - Location of the Conduits7. Disconnect the high and low-voltage connectors from the compressor (Figure 5).
title: RP-01-13-00-00-006 BTMS Compressor Replacement, p. 4

content_text: 1 LIONRepair Procedure: BTMS Compressor ReplacementPROCED. #:RP-01-13-00-00-006Publication Date: 2023-05-16Page 5 of 7PROCEDURE (Continued)Figure 5 - Location of the Connectors8. Remove the three bolts, washers, and nuts that attach the compressor to its support (Figure 6). Put the hardware aside.Figure 6 - Location of the hardware
title: RP-01-13-00-00-006 BTMS Compressor Replacement, p. 5

content_text: E LIONRepair Procedure: BTMS Compressor ReplacementPROCED. #:RP-01-13-00-00-006Publication Date: 2023-05-16Page 6 of 7PROCEDURE (Continued)9. Remove the compressor.10. Remove the oil inside the compressor. Note the amount of oil that was removed.Installation!Warning Only use an approved type of oil in the compressor. Different types of oil cannot be mixed.11. In the new compressor, add the same amount of PAG (SP-A2) oil that was removed from the old compressor.12. Position the compressor to its location.13. Install the three bolts, washers, and nuts previously removed that secure the compressor. Tighten to 6 ft-lb (8 Nm).14. Reconnect the conduits to the compressor. Tighten the conduits as per Figure 7.31.7 ft-lb (43 Nm)45.7 ft-lb (62 Nm)Figure 7 - Conduits Torque
title: RP-01-13-00-00-006 BTMS Compressor Replacement, p. 6

content_text: 3 LIONRepair Procedure: BTMS Compressor ReplacementPROCED. #:RP-01-13-00-00-006Publication Date:2023-05-16Page 7 of 7PROCEDURE (Continued)15. Reconnect the high and low-voltage connectors.16. Fill the compressor with refrigerant gas as per RP-01-13-00-00-010 Adjustment of the BTMS.17. Reactivate the high-voltage circuit.18. Position the starter switch to "START".19. On the touchscreen, get access to the BTMS page.20. On the BTMS page select as follows:a) Cooling manual mode: Manualb) Cooling manual on/off: ONc) Compressor startup speed: At least 50%.21. Once the test is completed without any problem, revert all the settings of the BTMS page.22. Make sure the BTMS compressor works properly and no warning indicator or any codes appear on the display.23. If any problem occurs during the test, troubleshoot the cause.

content_text: D LIONRepair Procedure: Replacement of the ABS Control UnitPROCED. #: RP-01-35-00-00-003Publication Date:2022-10-13Page 2 of 4SAFETY PRECAUTIONSWhen working on the vehicle, make sure the starter switch is in the "OFF" position, the parking brake is set, and the tires are chocked. Before working under the vehicle, always place jack stands under the frame rails to ensure the vehicle cannot drop. Failure to follow these steps can cause serious injuries or death.Tools used when working near batteries or electrical connections must be certified to a rating of 1000 Vdc to prevent injuries from electric shock. Short circuits between components or wires must be avoided.MAINTENANCE REFERENCEThis procedure is done in conjunction with MP-01-35-00-00-009 ABS Inspection.DURATIONThe duration of the repair procedure is approximately 60 minutes.LIST OF MATERIAL· ABS module second-gen Smart Track P/N 12611034-00TOOLS· Mixed wrench· Ratchet wrench with appropriate sockets· Torque wrenchCONSUMABLES· Brake liquid DOT 3

content_text: 4 LIONRepair Procedure: Replacement of the ABS Control UnitPROCED. #:RP-01-35-00-00-003Publication Date:2022-10-13Page 3 of 4PROCEDURE1. Make sure the work can be done safely.2. Make sure the vehicle is on a flat surface.3. Remove the brake fluid from the braking system.Removal4. Get under the vehicle and locate the ABS control unit (Figure 2).SECTION 2SECTION 3SECTION 4SECTION 5SECTION 6Figure 2 - Location of the ABS Control Unit5. Properly identify all the hydraulic brake lines that are connected to the unit and disconnect them.6. Disconnect the connector from the unit.7. Remove the hardware that attaches the unit to the vehicle (Figure 3).
title: RP-01-35-00-00-003 Remplacement of the ABS Control Unit, p. 3

document_title: RP-01-35-00-00-003 Remplacement of the ABS Control Unit.pdf
content_text: D LIONRepair Procedure: Replacement of the ABS Control UnitPROCED. #: RP-01-35-00-00-003Publication Date: 2022-10-13Page 4 of 4PROCEDURE (Continued)02XFigure 3 - Location of Hardware8. Remove the ABS control unit.Installation9. Position the ABS control unit to its location.10. Install the hardware that attaches the unit to the vehicle. Tighten the nuts to 180 ft-lb (244 Nm).11. Install all the hydraulic lines to their proper location on the unit. Tighten the connectors to 13.2 ft-lb (18 Nm).12. Add new brake fluid to the brake fluid reservoir.13. Bleed the braking system as per RP-01-35-01-00-0-06 Replacement of the Brake Calipers (Hydraulic).14. Position the starter switch to "START".15. Make sure the ABS indicator light disappeared after 3 seconds. If the indicator light remains on, bring the vehicle to a speed of 4 mph (6 km/h). The indicator light should be off.16. If the indicator light remains on, troubleshoot the ABS.17. Proceed to a road test before releasing the vehicle.
